transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. I'm here because... well, for a long time now, my sleep has just been really broken. I fall into bed completely exhausted, but then I wake up to every little sound in the house. And then I'm usually up before the alarm even goes off, just feeling like I never really rested at all.
Do you find that you spend a lot of your time worrying excessively about various things in your daily life, such as your job, your health, or your finances?

No, I don't really do that. I mean, I think about my patients at work sometimes, or making sure the bills are paid, but... no, I wouldn't say I worry excessively about it. My mind isn't really racing with all those kinds of thoughts. I'm just not a big worrier.
Over the past few weeks, have you felt a loss of interest or pleasure in doing the things you usually enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I'm definitely tired from not sleeping well, so sometimes I just don't have the energy to do much after work. But... no, I still enjoy the things I usually like doing. I haven't lost interest in them or anything like that.
Do you find yourself falling asleep during the day, or do you take naps?
No, I don't really nap. I mean, I'm definitely tired during the day, especially when I'm at work with my patients, but I don't fall asleep. I just kind of push through it.
Has anyone ever mentioned to you that you snore loudly or that you seem to stop breathing or gasp for air while you are asleep?

No, no one's ever said anything like that. I live alone anyway, so there's really no one around to tell me if I snore or do anything weird like that while I'm sleeping. But as far as I know, no, nothing like that.
When you first get into bed at night, do you typically fall asleep quickly, or does it take you a long time to drift off?

Well, falling asleep isn't really the issue. I fall into bed exhausted, so I usually drift off pretty quickly. The problem is that my sleep is just... broken. I wake up to every little sound in the house, and then I'm up way before my alarm even goes off. When I finally get out of bed, I feel like I never really rested at all. It's been like this for a long time now.

When you wake up before your alarm, is it because you are experiencing a specific physical discomfort, like pain or a need to use the bathroom, or do you just wake up and find yourself unable to fall back asleep?

No, it's not because I'm in pain or need to use the bathroom or anything like that. I just... wake up. My eyes open, and I'm just awake. I lie there trying to go back to sleep, but my mind is just kind of going, and I can't drift off again. So I just end up lying there until it's time to get up.
When you wake up in the middle of the night, how long does it typically take you to fall back asleep?

I don't really know exactly. Like I mentioned, a lot of times I just don't fall back asleep at all. If I do manage to drift off again, I couldn't tell you how long it takes... I try not to look at the clock because it just makes me more frustrated. It just feels like I'm lying there in the dark for hours.
Are you currently taking any medications, supplements, or substances like caffeine or alcohol that might be affecting your sleep?

No, I don't take anything like that. I don't take any sleeping pills or supplements, and I'm not on any other medications right now. I have a cup of coffee in the morning before work, but that's it. And I don't really drink alcohol, maybe just a glass of wine on a holiday or something, but definitely not on a regular basis. So I don't think it's anything I'm taking that's causing this.
How many months or years has this pattern of waking up early and being unable to fall back asleep been happening?
It's been... well, it started right around the time my mother-in-law moved in with us. That was a little over two years ago now. So it's been happening since then.
When you wake up early and find yourself unable to fall back asleep, do you feel physically alert and energetic, or do you still feel physically tired and exhausted?

I still feel very tired. I'm definitely not waking up feeling alert or refreshed. It's more like a constant exhaustion that just stays with me all day. 

By the time I finish seeing my home-health clients and come back to help out at my own house... my body just feels so heavy. It gets to the point where even just charting my work notes or folding some laundry can feel like too much to push through.

Since your mother-in-law moved in two years ago, has there been any period where the sleep difficulties stopped or significantly improved, or has this pattern been consistent every single night since it began?

No, not really. It's been pretty consistent the whole time. I mean, maybe there's a random night here or there where I manage to sleep a little bit longer, but... no, there hasn't been any period where it actually stopped or got better. It's just been an everyday thing for the last two years.
When you are away from home, such as when you are traveling or staying elsewhere, do you find that your sleep improves at all?

I... well, I actually don't know. I haven't really traveled or stayed anywhere else since she moved in. Between work and helping out at the house, there just hasn't been an opportunity to go anywhere overnight, so I haven't been able to see if being away makes a difference.
When you are in your own bed at home, do you find that you feel more tense or alert as soon as you lie down, even if you were feeling sleepy while sitting on the couch just moments before?

I don't really think so. I mean, I'm always exhausted, so when I get into bed, I just feel tired like I always do. I don't suddenly feel wide awake or tense or anything. I just... I lie there feeling heavy and worn out, but I still can't seem to stay asleep.
When you are lying awake in the middle of the night, does your mind tend to focus on the fact that you are awake and worry about the consequences of not getting enough sleep?

No, I wouldn't say I worry about the sleep itself. I mean, I know I'll be tired the next day, but that's just how it is now. When I wake up, my mind usually just goes straight to all the things I have to do... making sure my mother-in-law is okay, getting ready for my shifts, all the chores. It's more about feeling overwhelmed by everything I have to handle rather than stressing over the fact that I'm awake.
When you are lying awake at night thinking about your responsibilities, do you feel a sense of physical tension in your body, such as tight muscles or a racing heart?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My heart doesn't race or anything. I don't think my muscles get tight, either... it's really just that heavy, tired feeling I mentioned before. My body just feels completely exhausted, even if my mind is stuck running through my to-do list.

If you look back at your sleep over the last two years, do you find that you have more difficulty falling asleep initially at the start of the night, or is your main problem specifically staying asleep once you have drifted off?

It's definitely staying asleep. For a long time now, my sleep has just been... broken. 

Like I said, I fall into bed completely exhausted, so dropping off at the start of the night isn't really the issue. But after that, I just wake up to every little sound in the house. And then I'm usually up for good before my alarm even goes off, feeling like I never really rested at all.

When you wake up in the middle of the night, is your inability to return to sleep primarily caused by the environmental noise in your home, or do you find that you remain awake even when the house is completely quiet?

I think it happens even when the house is completely quiet. A little noise might be what wakes me up in the first place, but... once I'm awake, I'm awake. The house can be dead silent after that, and I'll still just be lying there, stuck thinking about everything I have to get done. So it's not really the noise keeping me from going back to sleep.
